brief.summary: High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (FPS) from HIRES/UVES and XQ-100 at z~4-5 provides the strongest small-scale structure probe of warm/sterile dark matter, with published thermal-relic limits m_th >5.3-5.7 keV from hydrodynamical simulations plus Bayesian/emulator inference. The signal is a scale-dependent suppression on small scales and modest enhancement on large scales in WDM vs CDM, highly degenerate with IGM thermal history (T0(z), gamma, pressure smoothing scale, mean flux, patchy reionization). Recent Gaussian-process emulators (Bird et al. LaCE, Lyssa Nyx 4096^3 120 Mpc suite, Sherwood-Relics) interpolate FPS over cosmology and IGM parameters, enabling MCMC constraints but with emulator error and prior dependence. Sterile-neutrino dark matter limits map m_th to m_s via production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow vs resonant Shi-Fuller vs diluted), and are complemented by X-ray decay line (E=m_s/2) and BBN N_eff/Yp/D/H bounds, with mixed cold+warm models reopening keV-scale parameter space and creating tension with 0.6-1.6 keV warmness claims from other probes.

delta:
**Survey.** The team found 32 tools on 3 servers and 3 relevant papers, and ran 6 read-only probes.

High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (FPS) from HIRES/UVES and XQ-100 at z~4-5 provides the strongest small-scale structure probe of warm/sterile dark matter, with published thermal-relic limits m_th >5.3-5.7 keV from hydrodynamical simulations plus Bayesian/emulator inference. The signal is a scale-dependent suppression on small scales and modest enhancement on large scales in WDM vs CDM, highly degenerate with IGM thermal history (T0(z), gamma, pressure smoothing scale, mean flux, patchy reionization). Recent Gaussian-process emulators (Bird et al. LaCE, Lyssa Nyx 4096^3 120 Mpc suite, Sherwood-Relics) interpolate FPS over cosmology and IGM parameters, enabling MCMC constraints but with emulator error and prior dependence. Sterile-neutrino dark matter limits map m_th to m_s via production mechanism (Dodelson-Widrow vs resonant Shi-Fuller vs diluted), and are complemented by X-ray decay line (E=m_s/2) and BBN N_eff/Yp/D/H bounds, with mixed cold+warm models reopening keV-scale parameter space and creating tension with 0.6-1.6 keV warmness claims from other probes.

The plan should check:
- Thermal-relic mass lower bound m_th (keV) and half-mode scale k_1/2 / free-streaming length.
- Sterile neutrino mass m_s and mixing sin^2(2theta) mapping from m_th for Dodelson-Widrow and resonant production.
- 1D flux power spectrum P_F(k,z) suppression factor vs CDM at k~0.01-0.1 s/km, z=4.2-5.0.
- IGM thermal parameters T0(z), gamma, pressure smoothing lambda_P, mean transmitted flux <F> and reionization history.
- Matter power amplitude and slope on small scales and N_eff, Yp, D/H shifts from sterile thermalization.
- X-ray decay line energy E=m_s/2 and flux vs existing X-ray limits to contrast with Lyman-alpha structure limits.

---
name: literature-research
description: Literature-grounded research on any physics topic: search strategy, reading discipline, citations, and published figures
---

Use this whenever published results matter — collider physics, neutrinos,
astroparticle, nuclear, cosmology alike. The method is identical in every
sub-field; do not reserve it for topics that look "researchy". A detector
explainer needs citations exactly as much as a cosmology analysis.

SEARCH:
- Query with 2-3 short keyword phrases, not full sentences — long phrase
  queries return junk (sometimes the SAME irrelevant paper for every
  variation; that is the search failing, not the literature missing).
- If the canonical paper is already known, skip search and go straight to
  its arXiv ID — the download/read tools take IDs directly.
- Nothing after 2-3 distinct keyword sets: say so and move on; do not
  keep permuting queries.

READ:
- Read papers in targeted sections (abstract, the relevant section, the
  figure captions) and distill findings into brief notes IMMEDIATELY.
  Never hold multiple full paper texts in context — full-text dumps have
  crashed real runs by overflowing the model's context window.

CITE:
- Every claim taken from a paper carries its arXiv ID or DOI. Uncited
  "well-known facts" are where wrong attributions slip in.

PUBLISHED FIGURES:
- Show a figure only with its caption and citation. Address figures by
  the PAPER's own numbering (the extractor reports it — trust that over
  file order). Extraction fails for many older / PDF-only papers; report
  that honestly — the fallback is downloading the PDF and extracting
  pages with a coding task.
- If the user names a figure you cannot resolve after ~2 lookups, ask one
  clarifying question instead of guessing across papers — and complete
  the unambiguous parts of the request meanwhile.

CLOSE THE LOOP: when compute tools can reproduce a published curve or
number, do it and compare — state explicitly what was and was not
reproduced, and why.

result.summary: Direction d-14 asked to deepen the Dodelson-Widrow (non-resonant production) sterile-neutrino mass mapping and the X-ray versus Lyman-alpha binding constraint for 100% sterile-neutrino dark matter. What was established: the sterile-neutrino server models DW and Shi-Fuller resonant (SF, with lepton asymmetry L) production, with Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN, light-element abundances Yp and D/H) fit valid for N_eff 2.044-6.044 and m_s below ~100 keV. A DW grid at sin^2(2theta)=1e-12 gave Omega_s h^2 (relic density in units of critical density) 0.00047 at 7.1 keV, 0.00304 at 20 keV, 0.00361 at 22 keV, 0.00594 at 29 keV, 0.0131 at 45 keV, implying f_s=1 (100% dark matter) mixings 2.5e-10, 3.9e-11, 3.3e-11, 2.0e-11, 9.2e-12 respectively (for observed Omega_DM h^2=0.12), with Delta N_eff 6e-6 to 2.7e-5 and BBN Delta chi^2 ~0 (allowed). File: /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-lyman-wdm/runs/261107_185835/sterile_nu_grid_DW_bc0526.csv. The 3.5 keV line benchmark (m_s=7.1 keV, sin^2 2theta=7e-11, DW) produces Delta N_eff=0.00043 (N_eff=3.0444), Omega_s h^2=0.033 (27.5% of dark matter), Yp=0.2468 (observed 0.2449 +/-0.004) and D/H=2.44e-5 (observed 2.547 +/-0.025e-5) with BBN Delta chi^2=-0.01 (allowed), photon energy E=m_s/2=3.55 keV, radiative lifetime 5.8e27 s (1.8e20 yr), free-streaming length 151 kpc, and is flagged excluded by NuSTAR M31 (Roach+2020) and XMM-Newton blank sky (Dessert+2020) in the tool's 10-limit database. A contrasting SF grid at same masses and mixing gave Omega_s h^2 6.17 to 248, all overclosing by 50-2000x, with heuristic Delta N_eff 0.1x DW (6e-7 to 2.7e-6). File: /Users/nramachandra/hep-genesis-testing/projects/ramp-research-lyman-wdm/runs/261107_185835/sterile_nu_grid_SF_ec8837.csv. ---
name: literature-research
description: Literature-grounded research on any physics topic: search strategy, reading discipline, citations, and published figures
---

Use this whenever published results matter — collider physics, neutrinos,
astroparticle, nuclear, cosmology alike. The method is identical in every
sub-field; do not reserve it for topics that look "researchy". A detector
explainer needs citations exactly as much as a cosmology analysis.

SEARCH:
- Query with 2-3 short keyword phrases, not full sentences — long phrase
  queries return junk (sometimes the SAME irrelevant paper for every
  variation; that is the search failing, not the literature missing).
- If the canonical paper is already known, skip search and go straight to
  its arXiv ID — the download/read tools take IDs directly.
- Nothing after 2-3 distinct keyword sets: say so and move on; do not
  keep permuting queries.

READ:
- Read papers in targeted sections (abstract, the relevant section, the
  figure captions) and distill findings into brief notes IMMEDIATELY.
  Never hold multiple full paper texts in context — full-text dumps have
  crashed real runs by overflowing the model's context window.

CITE:
- Every claim taken from a paper carries its arXiv ID or DOI. Uncited
  "well-known facts" are where wrong attributions slip in.

PUBLISHED FIGURES:
- Show a figure only with its caption and citation. Address figures by
  the PAPER's own numbering (the extractor reports it — trust that over
  file order). Extraction fails for many older / PDF-only papers; report
  that honestly — the fallback is downloading the PDF and extracting
  pages with a coding task.
- If the user names a figure you cannot resolve after ~2 lookups, ask one
  clarifying question instead of guessing across papers — and complete
  the unambiguous parts of the request meanwhile.

CLOSE THE LOOP: when compute tools can reproduce a published curve or
number, do it and compare — state explicitly what was and was not
reproduced, and why.

We revisit Lyman- α bounds on the dark matter mass in Λ Warm Dark
Matter (ΛWDM) models, and derive new bounds in the case of mix ed Cold plus
Warm models (ΛCWDM), using a set up which is a good approximat ion for

Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We pay a special attention to syste matics, test
various possible sources of error, and compare the results o f diﬀerent statistical
approaches. Expressed in terms of the mass of a non-resonant ly produced
sterile neutrino, our bounds read mnrp ≥ 8 keV (frequentist 99.7% conﬁdence

(frequentist 99.7% conﬁdence limit); similarly, the Bayes ian joint probability
on ( Fwdm, 1/m nrp) allows any value of the mass at the 95% conﬁdence level,

Abstract
We revisit Lyman- α bounds on the dark matter mass in Λ Warm Dark
Matter (ΛWDM) models, and derive new bounds in the case of mix ed Cold plus
Warm models (ΛCWDM), using a set up which is a good approximat ion for
several theoretically well-motivated dark matter models. We combine WMAP5
results with two diﬀerent Lyman- α data sets, including observations from the
Sloan Digital Sky Survey. We pay a special attention to syste matics, test
various possible sources of error, and compare the results o f diﬀerent statistical
approaches. Expressed in terms of the mass of a non-resonant ly produced
sterile neutrino, our bounds read mnrp ≥ 8 keV (frequentist 99.7% conﬁdence
limit) or mnrp ≥ 12. 1 keV (Bayesian 95% credible interval) in the pure ΛWDM
limit. For the mixed model, we obtain limits on the mass as a fu nction of
the warm dark matter fraction Fwdm. Within the mass range studied here
(5 keV < m nrp < ∞), we ﬁnd that any mass value is allowed when Fwdm < 0. 6
(frequentist 99.7% conﬁdence limit); similarly, the Bayes ian joint probability
on ( Fwdm, 1/m nrp) allows any value of the mass at the 95% conﬁdence level,
provided that Fwdm < 0. 35.

range [ 43, 44, 41, 45, 46, 47] and GeV range [ 42].
The small strength of interaction of light super-WIMP parti cles usually implies
that: (i) they were never in thermal equilibrium in the early Universe ; and (ii) they
were produced deep in the radiation dominated epoch, while s till being relativistic
(unlike CDM). The latter property means that the density per turbation of these

particles are suppressed for scales below their free-streaming length,1 which aﬀects
structure formation on those scales. If the maximum free-st reaming length roughly
coincides with galaxy scales, the particles are called Warm Dark Matter (WDM), see
e.g. [ 48].
Currently, the best way to distinguish between WDM and CDM mo dels is the
analysis of Lyman- α (Ly-α ) forest data (for an introduction see e.g. [ 49, 50, 51]).
This method requires particular care. Part of the physics en tering into the Ly- α
analysis is not fully understood (for a recent review see [ 52]), and can be signiﬁcantly
inﬂuenced by DM particles (see e.g. [ 53, 54, 55, 56, 57, 58, 59]). The results can
also be aﬀected by approximations related to computational diﬃculties. Indeed,
at the redshifts probed by Ly- α data, structures are already undergoing non-linear
evolution. In order to relate the measured ﬂux spectrum with the parameters of
each cosmological model, one would have to perform a prohibi tively large number
of numerical simulations. Therefore, various simplifying approximations have to be
realized. Diﬀerent approaches are presented in [ 60, 61, 62].
Previous works analyzing Ly- α constrains on WDM [ 63, 65, 64, 66, 67, 68] as-
sumed the simplest ΛWDM model with a cut-oﬀ in the linear powe r spectrum (PS)
of matter density ﬂuctuations. Such a PS arises when WDM part icles are ther-
mal relics . However, in many super-weakly interacting DM models, the P S has a
complicated non-universal form due to the non-thermal prim ordial velocity distri-
bution (see e.g. [ 69, 70, 71, 72]). For example, in gravitino models with broken
R-parity, gravitino production occurs in two stages: therm ally at high temperatures
(see e.g. [ 73, 74, 75]), and then non-thermally through the late decay of the next -to-
lightest supersymmetric particle (see e.g. [ 76, 69]). Therefore the primordial velocity
distribution results from the superimposition of a colder ( resonant) and a warmer
(thermal) component, and the PS is characterized by a step an d a plateau on small
scales (rather than a sharp cut-oﬀ).
Another interesting super-WIMP WDM model with a non-trivia l PS is the sterile
neutrino DM of the ν MSM– an extension of the SM by three sterile (right-handed,
gauge singlet) neutrinos [ 77, 78]. Having masses of all new particles below the electro-
weak scale, this model is able to explain simultaneously thr ee BSM phenomena:
(i) the transition between the neutrino of diﬀerent ﬂavours ( neutrino oscillations );
(ii) the production of a non-zero baryon number in the early Unive rse; and (iii) the
existence of DM candidate with correct relic density. 2 Sterile neutrino DM in the
ν MSM is produced via its mixing with active neutrinos in the ea rly Universe [ 15,

Therefore, in this work, apart from updating existing bound s on ΛWDM models, we
consider Ly- α bounds in the ΛCWDM scenario, including a mixture of a CDM and
WDM. This model is characterized by two independent paramet ers beyond the usual
dark matter fraction Ω DM: the velocity dispersion (or free-streaming length) of the
WDM component, and the fraction of WDM density. We will overv iew and provide
a critical analysis of uncertainties in the Ly- α method for this model, and derive
constraints on the above parameters. Finally, we will discu ss the consequences of
these results for some physically relevant DM models of this kind.
The ﬁrst qualitative analysis of Ly- α bounds in the ΛCWDM scenario was per-
formed in [ 94]. In this work, the authors computed the linear ΛCWDM power
spectra projected along the line of sight. The PS suppressio n (as compared to the
pure ΛCDM case) at some ﬁducial scale was compared with that q uoted in [ 66] for
several WDM masses. A ΛCWDM model was considered as ruled out at some con-

pure ΛWDM model ruled out at the same level in [ 66].
This qualitative method should be improved in two direction s. First of all, the
Ly-α method provides a measurement of the 1D non-linear ﬂux spectrum. The non-
linear evolution “mixes” diﬀerent scales. Therefore, two l inear PS passing through
the same point at a given wave number but having a diﬀerent beh avior otherwise
would ﬁt Ly- α data diﬀerently. Secondly, the eﬀects of CWDM suppression o n the
matter PS can be somewhat compensated by the change of cosmol ogical parameters
(DM abundances, σ 8, etc.). Therefore, a proper Ly- α analysis should include a
simultaneous ﬁtting of all cosmological plus CWDM paramete rs to the Ly- α (and
possibly other cosmological) data. Such an analysis is perf ormed in this work.

the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) data complied in Ref. [ 96, 61]. In section 4,
we discuss the issue of including thermal velocities in hydr odynamical simulations

# Lyman-alpha forest constraints on warm and sterile-neutrino dark matter: IGM prior and emulator robustness, and complementarity with BBN and X-ray limits

## Abstract
High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (FPS, the variance of transmitted flux as a function of line-of-sight wavenumber) at $z = 4.2-5.0$ gives $m_{\rm th} > 5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ at 95% confidence for a thermal-relic warm dark matter (WDM, particles with keV-scale mass and appreciable free-streaming) particle, with $m_{\rm th} > 5.3\,\mathrm{keV}$ from earlier XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE data. The bound is degenerate with intergalactic medium (IGM, diffuse hydrogen between galaxies) thermal history and emulator interpolation error, and its detailed dependence on $k_{\rm max}$, $T_0(z)$ (temperature at mean density), $\gamma$ (slope of the temperature-density relation), pressure smoothing and patchy reionization was not quote-verified in this run. For Dodelson-Widrow (DW, non-resonant production via active-sterile mixing) sterile neutrinos the tool predicts negligible Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN, light-element formation) shifts at 100% dark matter mixings, so structure and X-ray decay limits dominate, while Shi-Fuller (SF, resonant production with lepton asymmetry) overcloses by $50-2000\times$ at the same mixings. Mixed cold plus warm dark matter (CWDM, a fraction $f_{\rm WDM}$ of warm component) reopens low-mass parameter space excluded for pure WDM.

## Background
The literature reports thermal-relic limits $m_{\rm th} > 5.3-5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ from hydrodynamical simulations plus Bayesian or emulator inference applied to HIRES/UVES and XQ-100 FPS at $z \sim 4-5$. The signal is a scale-dependent suppression on small scales and modest enhancement on large scales in WDM versus cold dark matter (CDM, effectively zero free-streaming) (arXiv:2209.09895). Gaussian-process emulators interpolate $P_F(k,z)$ (1D flux power spectrum) over cosmology and IGM parameters, enabling Markov Chain Monte

Carlo constraints but with emulator error and prior dependence (arXiv:2011.15127, arXiv:2305.19064). Sterile-neutrino dark matter limits map $m_{\rm th}$ to $m_s$ (sterile-neutrino mass) via production mechanism, and are complemented by X-ray decay line $E = m_s/2$ and BBN $N_{\rm eff}$ (effective number of relativistic species), $Y_p$ (helium mass fraction) and $D/H$ (deuterium to hydrogen ratio) bounds, with mixed models reopening keV-scale space (arXiv:0812.0010, arXiv:2504.06367). Recent NuSTAR Milky Way halo searches set $\sin^2(2\theta)$ (active-sterile mixing angle) limits for $m_s = 6-40\,\mathrm{keV}$ (arXiv:2207.04572).

## Results

### Thermal-relic bound and its reported sensitivity to IGM priors
High-resolution data at $z = 4.2-5.0$ from HIRES/UVES give $m_{\rm th} > 5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ at 95% confidence (2 sigma) in Irsic et al. 2023 (arXiv:2309.04533) and $m_{\rm th} > 5.3\,\mathrm{keV}$ in Irsic et al. 2017 (arXiv:1702.01764). The literature spread $3.1-5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ is attributed to maximum wavenumber $k_{\rm max}$ cut and $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ prior choices. This attribution is not independently verified in this run because verbatim quotes for $k_{\rm max}$, redshift range, $T_0(z)$, $\gamma$, pressure smoothing scale $\lambda_P$, mean transmitted flux $\langle F \rangle$ and patchy reionization assumptions could not be extracted before the tool budget was exhausted.

[[FIGURE 36]]
Figure 36. Two-dimensional posterior distributions for XQ-100, HIRES/MIKE and combined data sets showing dependence on thermal history parametrization.

The figure shows marginalized posteriors for the main parameters, illustrating how different thermal-history treatments shift contours. No numerical table of $k_{\rm max} = 0.1$ versus $0.2\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$ or $T_0(z)$ power-law versus free-floating versus $5000\,\mathrm{K}$ jump priors was recovered.

### Emulator systematics: LaCE versus Sherwood-Relics
Two contrasting emulators were compared at architecture l

evel. LaCE (Lyman-alpha Cosmology Emulator) is a Gaussian-process emulator that interpolates $P_F(k,z)$ over small-scale linear power amplitude and slope and IGM state at $2 < z < 4$ with $\sim 1\%$ accuracy on linear $P(k)$ rescaling, using $270$ training points in a Latin hypercube (arXiv:2011.15127, updated arXiv:2305.19064). Sherwood-Relics CWDM emulator uses a $20\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ box with $2\times1024^3$ dark matter and gas particles run with P-Gadget3 at $z = 4.2, 4.6, 5.0$, with a 10-fold cross-validated neural network predicting $16$ $k$-bins per redshift (arXiv:2504.06367).

[[FIGURE 37]]
Figure 37. Information compression for extended LambdaCDM showing ratio of $z=3$ linear matter power to baseline, rescaled at $k_p = 0.7\,\mathrm{Mpc^{-1}}$.

[[FIGURE 38]]
Figure 38. Distribution of 270 LaCE training points in 2D projections, colored by redshift for illustration.

[[FIGURE 46]]
Figure 46. Architecture of the mixture density network used in the updated LaCE emulator with six input parameters and Leaky-ReLU activations.

[[FIGURE 47]]
Figure 47. Distribution of training, central and reionization simulations in emulation parameter space showing coverage of reionization models.

[[FIGURE 48]]
Figure 48. Slice through Sherwood-Relics $20\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ simulation at $z=4.2$ showing gas and dark matter for CDM versus $1\,\mathrm{keV}$ and $3\,\mathrm{keV}$ WDM.

[[FIGURE 49]]
Figure 49. Emulator building process with k-fold cross-validation and neural network trained on each fold.

Quantitative leave-one-out interpolation error at $k = 0.01-0.1\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$, $z = 4.2-5.0$ in percent and propagated shift in keV on $m_{\rm th}$ was not extracted because full-text tables were not readable without cached PDFs. A preliminary low-confidence estimate that percent-level $P_F(k,z)$ error propagates to $0.2-0.5\,\mathrm{keV}$ shift and that widening $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ priors or cutting $k_{\rm max}$ from $0.2$ to $0.1\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$ each

loosens the bound by $0.5-1\,\mathrm{keV}$ remains not independently verified and relies on a proxy mapping.

### Dodelson-Widrow sterile-neutrino relic density and BBN complementarity
The sterile-neutrino server models DW and SF production, with BBN fit valid for $N_{\rm eff} = 2.044-6.044$ and $m_s \lesssim 100\,\mathrm{keV}$. All calculations ran locally; no facility dispatch was used. A DW grid at $\sin^2(2\theta) = 1\times10^{-12}$ gave:

| $m_s$ ($\mathrm{keV}$) | $\Omega_s h^2$ (relic density) | $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ (extra radiation) | $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN}$ | $f_s=1$ mixing $\sin^2(2\theta)$ for $\Omega_{\rm DM}h^2 = 0.12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $7.1$ | $0.00047$ | $6.2\times10^{-6}$ | $\sim 0$ | $2.5\times10^{-10}$ |

| $29$ | $0.00594$ | $2.0\times10^{-5}$ | $\sim 0$ | $2.0\times10^{-11}$ |

# Lyman-alpha forest constraints on warm and sterile-neutrino dark matter: IGM prior and emulator robustness, and complementarity with BBN and X-ray limits

## Abstract
High-resolution Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (FPS, the variance of transmitted flux as a function of line-of-sight wavenumber) at $z = 4.2-5.0$ gives $m_{\rm th} > 5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ at 95% confidence for a thermal-relic warm dark matter (WDM, particles with keV-scale mass and appreciable free-streaming) particle, with $m_{\rm th} > 5.3\,\mathrm{keV}$ from earlier XQ-100 plus HIRES/MIKE data. The bound is degenerate with intergalactic medium (IGM, diffuse hydrogen between galaxies) thermal history and emulator interpolation error, and its detailed dependence on $k_{\rm max}$, $T_0(z)$ (temperature at mean density), $\gamma$ (slope of the temperature-density relation), pressure smoothing and patchy reionization was not quote-verified in this run. For Dodelson-Widrow (DW, non-resonant production via active-sterile mixing) sterile neutrinos the tool predicts negligible Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN, light-element formation) shifts at 100% dark matter mixings, so structure and X-ray decay limits dominate, while Shi-Fuller (SF, resonant production with lepton asymmetry) overcloses by $50-2000\times$ at the same mixings. Mixed cold plus warm dark matter (CWDM, a fraction $f_{\rm WDM}$ of warm component) reopens low-mass parameter space excluded for pure WDM.

## Background
The literature reports thermal-relic limits $m_{\rm th} > 5.3-5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ from hydrodynamical simulations plus Bayesian or emulator inference applied to HIRES/UVES and XQ-100 FPS at $z \sim 4-5$. The signal is a scale-dependent suppression on small scales and modest enhancement on large scales in WDM versus cold dark matter (CDM, effectively zero free-streaming) (arXiv:2209.09895). Gaussian-process emulators interpolate $P_F(k,z)$ (1D flux power spectrum) over cosmology and IGM parameters, enabling Markov Chain Monte Carlo constraints but with emulator error and prior dependence (arXiv:2011.15127, arXiv:2305.19064). Sterile-neutrino dark matter limits map $m_{\rm th}$ to $m_s$ (sterile-neutrino mass) via production mechanism, and are complemented by X-ray decay line $E = m_s/2$ and BBN $N_{\rm eff}$ (effective number of relativistic species), $Y_p$ (helium mass fraction) and $D/H$ (deuterium to hydrogen ratio) bounds, with mixed models reopening keV-scale space (arXiv:0812.0010, arXiv:2504.06367). Recent NuSTAR Milky Way halo searches set $\sin^2(2\theta)$ (active-sterile mixing angle) limits for $m_s = 6-40\,\mathrm{keV}$ (arXiv:2207.04572).

### Thermal-relic bound and its reported sensitivity to IGM priors
High-resolution data at $z = 4.2-5.0$ from HIRES/UVES give $m_{\rm th} > 5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ at 95% confidence (2 sigma) in Irsic et al. 2023 (arXiv:2309.04533) and $m_{\rm th} > 5.3\,\mathrm{keV}$ in Irsic et al. 2017 (arXiv:1702.01764). The literature spread $3.1-5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ is attributed to maximum wavenumber $k_{\rm max}$ cut and $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ prior choices. This attribution is not independently verified in this run because verbatim quotes for $k_{\rm max}$, redshift range, $T_0(z)$, $\gamma$, pressure smoothing scale $\lambda_P$, mean transmitted flux $\langle F \rangle$ and patchy reionization assumptions could not be extracted before the tool budget was exhausted.

The figure shows marginalized posteriors for the main parameters, illustrating how different thermal-history treatments shift contours. No numerical table of $k_{\rm max} = 0.1$ versus $0.2\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$ or $T_0(z)$ power-law versus free-floating versus $5000\,\mathrm{K}$ jump priors was recovered.

### Emulator systematics: LaCE versus Sherwood-Relics
Two contrasting emulators were compared at architecture level. LaCE (Lyman-alpha Cosmology Emulator) is a Gaussian-process emulator that interpolates $P_F(k,z)$ over small-scale linear power amplitude and slope and IGM state at $2 < z < 4$ with $\sim 1\%$ accuracy on linear $P(k)$ rescaling, using $270$ training points in a Latin hypercube (arXiv:2011.15127, updated arXiv:2305.19064). For sterile neutrinos, BBN and relic density calculations agree that DW production at $f_s=1$ mixings produces negligible $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ and $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} \sim 0$, so BBN does not exclude 100% DW dark matter; structure and X-ray decay dominate. BBN alone excludes a fully thermalized sterile neutrino with $N_{\rm eff} = 4.044$ at $3.7\sigma$, because it predicts $Y_p = 0.2596$ and $D/H \times 10^5 = 2.777$ versus observed $Y_p = 0.2449 \pm 0.004$ and $D/H \times 10^5 = 2.547 \pm 0.025$, but this does not constrain DW $f_s = 1$ where $\Delta N_{\rm eff} < 0.0006$ and $\Delta\chi^2_{\rm BBN} \sim 0$.

The DW relic density grid and the SF contrast are high-confidence results from local server calculations, while the thermal-relic bound $m_{\rm th} > 5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ at $z = 4.2-5.0$ and the NuSTAR Milky Way halo limits for $m_s = 6-40\,\mathrm{keV}$ remain snippet-only and not independently verified against full text. The mixed cold plus warm dark matter loophole is supported by published transfer-function plateaus and 2D contours showing $F_{\rm WDM} < 0.6$ allowed at low masses and $F_{\rm WDM} < 0.35$ at $m \sim 5\,\mathrm{keV}$, but numerical $F_{\rm WDM}$ versus mass curves were not digitized. Emulator systematics are described at architecture level for LaCE with $270$ training points and $\sim 1\%$ linear power accuracy and for Sherwood-Relics with $20\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ $2\times1024^3$ simulations and 10-fold cross-validation, yet the claimed $0.2-0.5\,\mathrm{keV}$ shift on $m_{\rm th}$ and $0.5-1\,\mathrm{keV}$ loosening from $k_{\rm max} = 0.2$ to $0.1\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$ or from power-law to free-floating $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ priors rely on a proxy mapping and were flagged as not independently verified.

Several dead ends were encountered and explain missing numbers. Attempts to quote-verify the Viel 2005 coefficient $4.43\,\mathrm{keV}$ and the Abazajian 2006 normalization, to digitize X-ray $\sin^2(2\theta)$ versus $m_s$ curves at $7.1, 20, 22, 29, 45\,\mathrm{keV}$ from Roach et al. 2022, and to extract verbatim $k_{\rm max}$, $T_0(z)$, $\gamma$, $\lambda_P$, $\langle F \rangle$ and patchy reionization assumptions for Irsic et al. 2017 and 2023 all failed because arXiv HTML provided no extractable figures or tables and cached PDFs were absent. Quantitative leave-one-out $P_F(k,z)$ errors at $k = 0.01-0.1\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$, $z = 4.2-5.0$ and digitized CWDM exclusion curves from Sherwood-Relics were blocked for the same reason, and citation validation failed on LaTeX escaping. All sterile-neutrino grids and BBN impact plots ran locally on the hosted server, no high-performance computing facility dispatch was used, and web searches plus figure extraction were the only literature checks that succeeded before the tool budget was exhausted.

## Limitations
What could not be established reflects tool and budget limits rather than physics.

- The dependence of $m_{\rm th} > 5.3-5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ on $k_{\rm max}$ cut, $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ prior width, pressure smoothing $\lambda_P$, mean flux $\langle F \rangle$ and inhomogeneous reionization was not quote-verified because full-text reads returned file not found and no usable HTML existed for arXiv:2309.04533 and arXiv:1702.01764.
- Emulator interpolation error propagation to $m_{\rm th}$ in keV was not quantified because LaCE and Sherwood-Relics papers show architecture and coverage but do not quote percent errors at $k = 0.01-0.1\,\mathrm{s\,km^{-1}}$, $z = 4.2-5.0$ in captions, and full-text tables were unreadable.
- Numerical X-ray $\sin^2(2\theta)$ limits at $7.1, 20, 22, 29, 45\,\mathrm{keV}$ and the binding constraint $f_{s,\max}$ from X-ray versus Lyman-alpha mixed-DM were not digitized because Roach et al. 2022 is PDF-only with tikz figures dropped in conversion.
- The DW mass mapping spread between Viel $4.43\,\mathrm{keV}\,(m_{\rm th}/1\,\mathrm{keV})^{4/3}$, Abazajian and half-mode matchings, and the $3-16\times$ offset between tool $\Omega_s h^2$ and published normalizations, were not resolved because targeted reads timed out and the budget was exhausted.
- CWDM numerical bounds $F_{\rm WDM} < 0.6/0.35$ and $f_{\rm WDM} < 0.16, 0.35, 0.50, 0.67$ at $1-4\,\mathrm{keV}$ remain image-only, with no table data files to load and no Planck $N_{\rm eff}$ likelihood beyond BBN.

## Open directions
- Digitize NuSTAR and XMM-Newton $\sin^2(2\theta)$ versus $m_s$ curves at $7.1, 20, 22, 29, 45\,\mathrm{keV}$ to compute $f_{s,\max}$ from X-ray and determine whether X-ray alone excludes 100% DW dark matter.
- Quantify the $m_{\rm WDM}$ to $m_{s,{\rm DW}}$ mapping uncertainty by comparing Viel, Abazajian and half-mode matchings at fixed $m_{\rm th}$ to establish the $20$ to $45\,\mathrm{keV}$ floor spread in keV and percent.
- Re-extract Irsic et al. 2017 and 2023 likelihoods with documented $k_{\rm max}$, $T_0(z)$ and $\gamma$ priors, $\lambda_P$, $\langle F \rangle$ and patchy reionization treatments to measure the $3.1$ to $5.7\,\mathrm{keV}$ shift per systematic in keV.
- Apply the Viel mapping consistently to CWDM thermal-relic limits and test resonant Shi-Fuller production to quantify how much mixed models relax pure WDM bounds, up to factor $\sim 2$.
- Build a unified $m_s$ versus $\sin^2(2\theta)$ plane overlaying relic density $\Omega_s h^2 = 0.12$, free-streaming, X-ray decay and BBN $\Delta N_{\rm eff}$ constraints to show where 100% DW dark matter is simultaneously allowed.
